articles.desc: Recap: Australian wages grow at fastest pace in nearly 3 years, yet swaps see a 75% RBA peak Gold’s worst enemy right now is a 5% Treasury yield, not the headlines from the Middle East TSMC reportedly demands cash up front from AI chip clients amid circular financing fears Morgan Stanley sees USD/JP
articles.content: Recap: Australian wages grow at fastest pace in nearly 3 years, yet swaps see a 75% RBA peak Gold’s worst enemy right now is a 5% Treasury yield, not the headlines from the Middle East TSMC reportedly demands cash up front from AI chip clients amid circular financing fears Morgan Stanley sees USD/JPY fair value above 170, forecasts yen at 162 by late 2027 Recap: Japan exports hit record ¥11.8 trillion as AI chip demand extends run to 14 months What tokenized stock supply shows that price and volume miss: the Nvidia test Ueda keeps December hike in play as BOJ wants inflation anchored around 2% PBOC sets USD/ CNY mid-point today at 6.7118 (vs. estimate at 6.6654) Onchain investors bought Nvidia’s Huang sell-off: tokenized supply up 121% in a week Australian wages jump 1.1%, strongest since 2023, but real pay falls for a fourth quarter Japan’s trade deficit comes in at half the expected size as exports jump 20.5% Back to the future! Nvidia earnings/forecast lifts Nasdaq futures 1.3% Supplier, lender, shareholder: how Nvidia became the "Bank of AI" Nvidia’s missing 10-Q: three reasons to be alert, not alarmed Nvidia sees 75% revenue growth next year as Kress points to $2.5 trillion backlog Nvidia board shuts the door on Huang’s return, refuses to discuss his exit on call Oil: Private inventory survey shows a headline crude oil build vs. draw expected New Zealand producer prices rise again in Q3, though at a slower pace SEC reportedly probes Nvidia disclosures as Bessent demands answers within 10 days Nvidia hands three directors export control oversight days after Huang exit Nvidia (price up) tops forecasts by $7 billion as Kress steers first report since Huang exit US stocks fall; Dow stocks are the hardest hit with a drop of 1.65% investingLive Americas market news wrap: US retail sales continue to show resilience Summary: Nvidia: beat forecasts, guided Q4 revenue to $130bn and forecast about 75% growth in fiscal 2028. The board ruled out Huang’s return. Overhangs: a reported SEC probe, a delayed 10-Q and about $518bn in commitments. TSMC is reportedly seeking cash up front from some AI customers. Asian equities: SK Hynix rose about 4%, lifting the Kospi almost 2%. The Nikkei gained about 0.7%, the Hang Seng fell about 1.1%, and Nasdaq futures pared gains to around 0.7%. Gold: fell below $3,800 to a one-year low on Fed hike bets, and silver dropped almost 3%. Australia: wages rose 1.1% q/q and 3.5% y/y, the fastest in nearly three years, and swaps still see about a 75% chance the RBA has peaked. Japan: exports hit a record ¥11.8trn, and Ueda said rate hikes will continue. USD/JPY held near 159.4. Oil: Brent eased to around $92.65 and WTI to near $83.80. Nvidia set the tone for Asian trade on Wednesday, with results and a strong outlook lifting chip stocks across the region, while gold fell below $3,800 as markets braced for another Federal Reserve rate hike. Nvidia and equities Nvidia beat forecasts in its first report since Jensen Huang resigned as chief executive. Third-quarter revenue rose 103% to around $116 billion, and the company guided fourth-quarter revenue to $130 billion, above estimates of about $125 billion. On the earnings call, interim chief executive Colette Kress forecast revenue growth of about 75% in fiscal 2028, pointed to a cloud-industry backlog of $2.5 trillion, and said Nvidia intends to return all excess free cash flow to shareholders. Governance questions remain. Chairman Harvey Jones said the board does not intend to reinstate Huang and has hired Heidrick & Struggles to find a permanent chief executive. The Wall Street Journal reported that the Securities and Exchange Commission is investigating Nvidia, including whether its disclosures misled investors, and the company has not yet filed its quarterly 10-Q, breaking with past practice. Nvidia’s financial role in the AI industry is also under scrutiny, with total commitments of about $518 billion, according to the Financial Times. In contrast, TSMC is reportedly asking some AI chip customers to pay cash up front. Nasdaq 100 futures gave back part of their early gains and were up around 0.7%, with S&P 500 futures up about 0.3%. In Asia, South Korea’s memory makers led. SK Hynix rose about 4% and Samsung Electronics about 1.4%, lifting the Kospi almost 2%. Japan’s Nikkei 225 gained around 0.7%, although the broader Topix slipped, while the Hang Seng fell about 1.1% and the Shanghai Composite eased 0.4%. Gold Gold fell below $3,800 to its lowest in more than a year as markets priced in a near-certain December Fed hike. Spot gold was down about 1.5% at around $3,791 after touching a low near $3,781, and silver dropped almost 3% to around $46. With US 10-year yields near 5.1% and the dollar close to a 19-month high, the metal has lost support. Goldman Sachs has cut its end-2026 gold target to $4,150 from $4,650. Australia Australian wages rose 1.1% in the September quarter, the fastest pace in nearly three years, lifting annual growth to 3.5%. Award wage rises drove private sector pay and frontline workers lifted the public sector, but real wages fell for a fourth straight quarter. The result adds to the Reserve Bank of Australia’s inflation worries after a split vote lifted rates to 4.85% this month, yet swaps still imply about a 75% chance that rates have peaked. AUD/USD edged down to around 0.6724 ahead of Thursday’s jobs report. In New Zealand, producer price growth slowed in the third quarter, with input prices up 0.7% and output prices up 0.8%. Japan Japan’s exports rose for a 14th straight month to a record ¥11.8 trillion in October, up 20.5% on AI-related chip demand. Imports also set a record but rose less than expected, narrowing the trade deficit to around ¥477 billion. Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda said the bank will keep raising rates in line with economic and price developments, keeping a December hike in play. Morgan Stanley reiterated its preference for long USD/JPY, which held around 159.4 near Tokyo’s intervention line. The 10-year JGB yield was little changed near 2.87%. Oil Oil eased with Brent down about 0.5% at around $92.65 and WTI down about 1% near $83.80. Prices remain elevated because of the Iran war, which continues to drive Japan’s energy import bill and feed inflation pressure that keeps the Fed tightening. Ahead The minutes of the Fed’s October meeting are due later in the US session, followed by Australian jobs data on Thursday and Japan’s national inflation figures on Friday. This article was written by Eamonn Sheridan at investinglive.com.

articles.title: HSBC, TalkTalk, BBC Hit by Massive Cyberattack via Optimizely Malicious Code
articles.desc: HSBC, TalkTalk, and BBC customers warned after hackers exploit Optimizely to steal crypto and credit card data from 178 global organizations including IKEA and Zoom.
articles.content: HSBC, TalkTalk, BBC Hit by Massive Cyberattack via Optimizely Malicious Code | Technology HSBC, TalkTalk, BBC Hit by Massive Cyberattack via Optimizely Malicious Code HSBC, TalkTalk, and BBC customers warned after hackers exploit Optimizely to steal crypto and credit card data from 178 global organizations including IKEA and Zoom. and TalkTalk customers have been urgently instructed to update their Apple iPhones and review bank statements following a significant cyberattack that compromised hundreds of major global corporations. British security researchers identified the breach after discovering malicious code embedded within website management tools used by 178 international organizations. The attack specifically targeted , a widely used platform for testing website layouts, allowing hackers to inject harmful scripts into legitimate pages. How Hackers Exploited Optimizely Trusted Systems Optimizely confirmed that it has identified the vulnerability and removed the malicious code from its systems, but the method of delivery made detection exceptionally difficult for affected companies. Hackers did not need to breach the direct computer systems of banks, retail giants, or media outlets like the BBC. Instead, they exploited a weakness in the Optimizely platform to slip malicious instructions into the code. This code was then delivered to affected webpages through Optimizely's own trusted delivery system, appearing alongside genuine software updates. Optimizely Exploit Targets Major Brands Including BBC and Zoom This technique meant that visitors could encounter the threat simply by opening an affected webpage, without downloading an application or clicking on a suspicious email link. Report URI, a cyber security firm based in Lancashire, detected the attack yesterday evening after examining 1,611 Optimizely code files. Their analysis identified 188 infected files associated with 178 distinct organizations across various industries, exposing how even trusted digital infrastructure can be weaponized to steal personal data. Stakeholder Positions and Affected Global Entities The list of compromised entities is extensive and includes some of the most recognizable names in finance, technology, and retail. Major financial institutions affected include HSBC operations in the US, Hong Kong, Mexico, Singapore, Australia, the UAE, Malaysia, Taiwan, Vietnam, Egypt, and the Philippines. Other banking and finance victims include Equifax, Equifax Canada, Equifax UK, ABN AMRO, TaxAct, Funding Circle, and Hang Seng Investment. Telecom giant TalkTalk and public broadcaster BBC are among the British firms directly notified of the breach. Technology and retail sectors were also heavily impacted, with Zoom, Salesforce, IKEA, ASOS, Mattel, and Starbucks Canada among the affected organizations. The breadth of the attack highlights the interconnected nature of modern digital services. Researchers at Report URI worked to identify the scope of the breach, providing a comprehensive list of impacted sectors ranging from insurance providers like Admiral and Mutual of Omaha to home technology brands such as Honeywell Home and Chamberlain. This widespread notification ensures that diverse user bases across multiple continents are aware of the potential risk to their personal information. Real-World Impact on Consumers and Data Theft The malicious software deployed during the attack was designed with three primary objectives: stealing cryptocurrency payments, capturing credit card details entered into online forms, and hacking iPhones and iPads that had known security weaknesses. Early reports indicate that cryptocurrency transfers to wallets controlled by the attackers have amounted to little more than $7,000 (£5,20) so far. However, the total number of individuals whose card details were stolen or whose devices were successfully hacked remains unknown, creating a significant uncertainty for victims and financial institutions alike. PESB Chairperson gets another one-year extension — from leading TAFE to her key achievements The government has extended Srinivasan's tenure as PESB chairperson from November 19, 2026, to November 18, 2027, or until further orders. Mallika Srinivasan, Chairperson of the Public Enterprises Selection Board (PESB), has received a one-year extension as head of the government selection body. According to PSU Watch, the government has extended Srinivasan's tenure as PESB chairperson from November 19, 2026, to November 18, 2027, or until further orders. PESB is a Government of India body involved in selecting top-level executives for central public sector enterprises. Srinivasan is among India's prominent business leaders and has played a significant role in expanding 's presence in the domestic and global agricultural machinery markets. Widely known as the 'Tractor Queen of India', her career spans manufacturing, corporate leadership, industry bodies, education and philanthropy. She has also served on the boards of several prominent companies and institutions and received the Padma Shri in 2014 for her contribution to trade and industry. , one of the world's largest tractor manufacturers. She has led the company's growth and expansion across multiple business segments, including tractors, farm machinery, diesel engines, generators, engineering plastics, hydraulic pumps and cylinders, automobile franchises and plantations. TAFE has grown into a diversified business under her leadership, with revenues reportedly exceeding She has also served on the global board of the US-India Business Council (USIBC) and led the B20 India Task Force on 'Inclusive GVCs for Resilient Global Trade and Investment' in August 2023. Mallika Srinivasan's education and academic background graduated in mathematics from Women's Christian College in Chennai. She subsequently earned a university gold medal in econometrics from the University of Madras. She later graduated from the Wharton School of Business at the University of Pennsylvania, where she was a member of the Dean's Honor List and the Alpha Beta Gamma Society. Mallika Srinivasan's corporate leadership and board positions Srinivasan has been associated with several leading Indian companies and educational institutions in leadership and governance roles. - Tata Steel: Served as an independent director from 2012 to 2022. - Tata Global Beverages: Served as an independent director from 2008 to 2018. The company is now known as Tata Consumer Products. - Indian School of Business (ISB): Served on its executive board from 2002 to 2022. - IIT Madras: Served as a member of its governing board. She has also been associated with industry organisations, including the Tractor Manufacturers' Association of India and the Madras Chamber of Commerce. She has held positions in the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) and the Indian Institute of Foreign Trade. Her international engagements include her association with the US-India Business Council and the B20 India Task Force. articles.title: Cyberattack hits 178 organizations, targets website visitors
articles.desc: A cyberattack affected websites tied to 178 organizations. Las Vegas users can learn about the reported cryptocurrency and iPhone risks.
articles.content: Cyberattack hits 178 organizations, targets website visitors ) — A cyberattack involving a website optimization service exposed visitors to malicious code across sites linked to 178 organizations, including CNN and Zoom, Cybersecurity researcher Scott Helme discovered the attack Monday, according to TMZ. The outlet reported that hackers compromised Optimizely, a service companies use to improve their websites, allowing the code to spread to sites associated with organizations including the BBC, IKEA, Salesforce and Equifax. TMZ reported that visitors could be exposed simply by visiting an affected site, without clicking a suspicious link. Highly classified NSA communications network is down, report says The code was designed to replace cryptocurrency wallet addresses, potentially redirecting payments to the attackers, TMZ reported. According to the outlet, researchers said it also attempted to collect credit card information, browser cookies, and screenshots. The attack also attempted to exploit security flaws in older iPhones and iPads, TMZ reported. The outlet said there was no confirmed evidence that any iPhones were successfully infected. Helme identified 188 infected scripts tied to 178 organizations, according to TMZ. Researchers also found about $7,000 in transactions going to wallets associated with the scheme, the outlet reported, though it was unclear how much, if any, came from victims. TMZ reported that Optimizely said it had fixed the vulnerability and removed the malicious code from affected projects. Security experts urged users to keep their devices updated, according to the outlet. TMZ did not identify a Las Vegas-specific impact in its report. Copyright 2026 KVVU. All rights reserved. articles.title: ASI begins digitising ancient inscriptions at Tirumala temple
articles.desc: ASI begins digitising ancient inscriptions at Tirumala temple
articles.content: ASI begins digitising ancient inscriptions at Tirumala temple | Vijayawada News - The Times of India ASI begins digitising ancient inscriptions at Tirumala temple ASI begins digitising ancient inscriptions at Tirumala temple The ongoing exercise will be followed by a fresh documentation drive to copy and digitise the remaining inscriptions at the temple from Dec 1 The Archaeological Survey of India’s (ASI) epigraphy branch has begun digitising existing estampages (inked paper impressions) of inscriptions copied from the ‘prakara’ walls of the Sri Venkateswara temple as part of its flagship BharatSHRI (Bharat Shared Repository of Inscriptions) initiative. Nearly 100 centuries-old inscriptions documenting royal donations and temple rituals during the Vijayanagara era are being digitally preserved, with two records detailing gold offerings by the queens of emperor Krishnadevaraya offering a rare glimpse into 16th-century royal patronage at Tirumala. According to an official note issued by Dr K Munirathnam Reddy, ASI’s director of epigraphy, the ongoing exercise will be followed by a fresh documentation drive to copy and digitise the remaining inscriptions at the temple from Dec 1, following formal clearance from the Among the inscriptions currently being digitised, two engraved on the north wall of the temple’s first ‘prakara’ are of particular historical significance. Written in Telugu, they are dated Feb 10, 1513 CE. The inscriptions record elaborate ritual offerings made to Lord Tiruvengalanatha (Sri Venkateswara) by Chinnajiamma and Tirumalamma, queens of Vijayanagara emperor Krishnadevaraya. The royal endowment included two gold cups, each weighing 374 tukas, and a gold plate weighing 10 tukas, intended to hold perfumes. The vessels were meant for offering milk to the presiding deity after the night worship ritual, known as ‘ekanta seva’. The records are particularly significant as the donations were made during Krishnadevaraya’s first of seven documented visits to the hill shrine, shedding light on the religious practices, royal generosity and temple patronage of the Vijayanagara period. Once digitised, the high-resolution estampages, along with their transcripts and historical summaries, will be uploaded to the BharatSHRI online portal. The initiative aims to safeguard the country’s epigraphic heritage while making these historical records accessible to researchers, historians and the general public. articles.title: Xi urges China-Chile ties in AI, polar and deep-sea research
articles.desc: Xi urges China-Chile cooperation in AI, polar and deep-sea exploration
articles.content: Xi urges China-Chile cooperation in AI, polar and deep-sea exploration Xi urges China-Chile cooperation in AI, polar and deep-sea exploration The Shenzhen meeting follows Chile's new deal with OpenAI to train civil servants in artificial intelligence Delegations led by Chinese President Xi Jinping and Chile’s President Jose Antonio Kast attend a bilateral meeting on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen, Guangdong province, China Nov 17, 2026. REUTERS/Maxim Shemetov/Pool China and Chile should expand emerging cooperation in artificial intelligence, polar scientific expeditions and deep-sea exploration, Chinese President Xi Jinping told Chilean President Jose Antonio Kast on Tuesday, state media reported. Xi and Kast were speaking in the southern Chinese tech and manufacturing hub of Shenzhen ahead of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit. In a separate statement, Kast said emerging technologies also required clear regulatory frameworks. "We cannot fear artificial intelligence or quantum technology. We have to move forward, always with respect, with clear rules," Kast told reporters. US-based OpenAI and the Chilean government signed an agreement this week to train public servants in AI and explore its use in government services. Chile's Science Minister Ximena Lincolao and the company's Chief Executive Sam Altman met on Monday in San Francisco. Kast added that discussions with the Chinese president extended to trade, industry, infrastructure, mining and agriculture. Chile is the world's top copper producer and maintains a permanent presence in Antarctica. The Chilean president also underscored the importance of a planned meeting between the leaders of China, the United States and Russia at the summit, citing the impact major powers have on global geopolitics. "Every conflict that occurs worldwide seriously affects smaller nations like ours," Kast said. "Each of those events, no matter how distant from our nation, affects our quality of life, the cost of living." "That is why we so strongly value this opportunity for conversation, for dialogue that these three great nations will have," he added. articles.title: CD83 CAR T Cells Can Take the Reins When CD19 CAR T Cells Lose Their Punch
articles.desc: Roswell Park researchers found CD83 CAR T cells could overcome CD19-targeted therapy resistance in preclinical models of B-cell cancers.
articles.content: CD83 CAR T Cells Can Take the Reins When CD19 CAR T Cells Lose Their Punch | OncLive CD83 CAR T Cells Can Take the Reins When CD19 CAR T Cells Lose Their Punch CD19 antigen loss emerged as a key mechanism of resistance after CD19 CAR T in ALL models, motivating sequential or alternative antigen targeting strategies to restore cytotoxic activity. CD83 expression was observed across ALL, MCL, and DLBCL, while absent in CLL and circulating healthy B cells, supporting a potentially favorable therapeutic window. CD83 CAR T showed efficacy in vitro and in vivo as salvage after CD19-directed failure and as standalone therapy, indicating functional redundancy independent of CD19. Lower propensity for B-cell aplasia with CD83 CAR T suggests a differentiated toxicity profile versus CD19 CAR T, potentially mitigating infection-related nonrelapse mortality. Ongoing phase 1 evaluation of CD83 CAR T in relapsed/refractory AML (NCT06871410) is intended to generate safety data informing expansion into B-cell malignancy trials. Roswell Park researchers found CD83 CAR T cells could overcome CD19-targeted therapy resistance in preclinical models of B-cell cancers. CAR T-cell therapy targeting the cell-surface protein CD19 is the standard of care for aggressive B-cell malignancies that have relapsed or are treatment-resistant, and in some cases, it can result in a cure. But if the disease relapses after CD19 CAR T therapy, median overall survival is poor. Writing in the Journal for ImmunoTherapy of Cancer, a team from Roswell Park Comprehensive Cancer Center suggests a way to change that outcome. that CAR T therapy — short for chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy, an advanced form of cancer immunotherapy that reprograms a patient’s own immune cells to find and destroy cancer cells — that is designed to target a different protein, CD83, can renew the immune system’s attack against cancer cells when CD19 antigen loss reduces the effectiveness of CD19 CAR T. , Vice Chair of Strategic Initiatives in Cell Therapy at Roswell Park, and senior author , Senior Vice President and Associate Director for Translational Research at Roswell Park and a pioneer in the field of CAR T-cell therapy. Using both in vitro and in vivo preclinical models, the team evaluated CD83 expression in several B-cell malignancies, which affect the white blood cells that produce antibodies and help fight infection. They found that it is expressed in acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL), mantle cell lymphoma (MCL) and diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL), but not in chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) or circulating healthy B cells. Comparing the potency of both CD19 and CD83 CAR T cells, the researchers discovered that after B-cell ALL is treated with CD19 CAR T-cell therapy, loss of the CD19 antigen can make the treatment ineffective. “Even in cases where prior cell therapy has taken CD19 out of the equation, CD83 is still expressed and can serve as an alternate target,” says Dr. Betts. “That provides two routes for eradicating the cancer cells.” The team reports that CD83 CAR T was also effective when administered as a monotherapy in preclinical models. The researchers also found another benefit of CD83 CAR T therapy: B-cell aplasia, which leaves patients with an insufficient number of infection-fighting B lymphocytes, is a major cause of non-relapse-related death after CD19 CAR T, but CD83 CAR T is associated with a low risk of aplasia. ) offered exclusively at Roswell Park for patients with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) that has relapsed or is treatment-resistant. Investigators hope results of the trial will provide safety data to inform future clinical trials of CD83 CAR T for B-cell malignancies. “CAR T-cell therapy has revolutionized the treatment of blood cancers that have relapsed or are treatment-resistant, often leading to long-lasting remissions in patients who have limited options,” notes Dr. Davila. “CD83 offers a promising new target that could extend the bene

Isomorphic Labs said on Tuesday it has raised $5 billion in ​a Series C funding round co-led ‌by Greenoaks and Sequoia Capital, as the ​Alphabet-backed AI drug discovery company ⁠works to move its first drug candidates into clinical trials. The company, which was spun ‌out of Google DeepMind in 2021, declined to share its ‌valuation. The funding comes about ‌six months ⁠after it raised $2.1 billion in ⁠a Series B round led by Thrive Capital. * Andreessen Horowitz and other ​new investors joined ‌the round, while Alphabet made a significant investment and other existing backers, including Thrive, MGX and GV, also participated * "This ‌round enables us to accelerate ​our progress: building foundational biology models, deepening our systemic disease understanding, and ⁠driving our first therapeutic programs towards clinical trials to deliver tangible impact for patients," ‌Isomorphic founder and CEO Demis Hassabis said * The company is developing its IsoDDE drug design engine, which uses AI to design new drugs, predict their properties and refine them ‌before scientists decide on the candidates to ​make and test * Isomorphic said it has seen positive pre-clinical ⁠results in internal oncology and immunology programs and ⁠with partners, "setting the stage for clinical entry" * The company lists ‌Novartis, Eli Lilly and Johnson & Johnson as its partners, according to ​its website Comments have to be in English, and in full sentences. articles.title: Stockton University expands forensics lab as student interest grows
articles.desc: Stockton University students get hands-on crime scene training in an expanded forensics lab as interest in the field continues to grow.
articles.content: Stockton University expands forensics lab for students – NBC10 Philadelphia Stockton University expands forensics lab as student interest grows With a newly expanded forensics lab and hands-on training, Stockton University is preparing students to investigate real-world crimes. Students at Stockton University are getting their hands dirty as they learn how to investigate crime scenes, uncover evidence and potentially help solve real-world cases. Interest in forensic science is growing at the university, which recently expanded its forensics lab to give students more opportunities for hands-on training. Stream Philadelphia News for free, 24/7, wherever you are with NBC10. The expanded facility, which opened just a couple of months ago, includes a mock crime scene, an area for blood spatter analysis and equipment to examine fingerprints, hair and other evidence. "We needed to create a practical learning space where students can get messy," said Barbara LeClair, a criminal justice teaching specialist at Stockton University. That includes digging for evidence at simulated crime scenes, where students must work carefully to avoid damaging potentially critical clues. During one practice excavation, students searched a mock burial site, uncovering objects meant to replicate evidence investigators might encounter in a real case. "Even clothing we even saw that was inside the grave," said Nabil Choudhury, a junior at Stockton. Breaking news and the stories that matter to your neighborhood. LeBron James sues makers of AI sports-betting app ‘Bron' for using his likeness While the students weren't digging up actual human remains, the exercise offered a realistic look at the challenges forensic investigators face. "Seeing it and pulling things out of the ground, It's very different from looking at crime scene photos," said Bailey Kunz, a Stockton senior. LeClair said the goal is to prepare students for the pressures and responsibilities that come with investigating sensitive cases. "We want to throw them in the lion’s den here so they're prepared to handle these sensitive real-world cases so they don't make those errors when they get on to being the professional world," LeClair said. Philadelphia 'House of Horrors' case draws students' attention One investigation that has captured the attention of Stockton's forensic science students is Philadelphia's so-called "House of Horrors" case. Investigators recently spent days digging for evidence connected to missing women, an effort that has sparked interest among students learning about the techniques used in forensic investigations. "We’re all keeping up with the whole story. We want to find out. We kind of want to investigate with the investigators, help out with the knowledge that we have so far," said Nataly Cascro, a Stockton senior. The case highlights the importance of carefully collecting and analyzing evidence, skills students are practicing through their coursework and simulated investigations. The former FBI profiler who helped identify the "Unabomber" grew up blocks away from the "house of horrors" on Chew Avenue in Philadelphia's Olney neighborhood. He offers his take on Raymond "R.C." Horsch's psychological evaluation in an interview with NBC10 investigative reporter David Charns. Preparing the next generation of forensic investigators Advances in DNA technology and genetic genealogy are helping investigators solve cold cases that previously may have seemed impossible to crack. At Stockton, students are learning the fundamentals of evidence collection and crime scene analysis as they prepare for potential careers in the field. For some, the motivation goes beyond the science. It's about helping families find answers and justice. "It's kind of hard to like figure out what's going on. So like wanting to help people and help them get that answers and get them that justice," Kunz said. articles.content: Researchers at Rady Children’s Institute for Genomic Medicine found that rapid and ultra-rapid whole-genome sequencing yielded positive findings in 36.2% of adolescents tested. Eight of those findings could have been identified through a newborn genomic screening program, raising questions about opportunities for earlier diagnosis.
